stem: A study finds that cities with more cycle lanes have fewer road accidents, so the mayor plans more lanes to cut accidents. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Cycle lanes cost much less to build than flyovers do.
Many people in the city already own and use bicycles.
Those cities also have lower speed limits and stricter enforcement.
The mayor has also promised to plant more trees.
explanation: Other differences between the cities could explain the fewer accidents, so lanes may not be the cause. The other options are not about what causes accidents.

stem: The company's last two directors were from Lahore, and both resigned in the first year. The board decides that no one from Lahore can hold the post for long. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
treats a needed condition as if it were enough
draws a general claim from a very small group
explanation: Two cases cannot support a claim about everyone from Lahore.

stem: Either we cancel the school trip, or we let students travel without teachers. We cannot let them travel without teachers, so we must cancel the trip. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
draws a general claim from a very small group
offers only two choices when more are possible
treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
explanation: There are other options, such as sending teachers with them or changing the destination.

stem: A farmer will sow wheat two weeks earlier this year so that the crop is harvested before the monsoon rains. The farmer assumes that
options: other farmers will also sow two weeks earlier than usual.
the price of wheat will rise before the monsoon arrives.
the farmer will need extra labour at harvest time.
the rains will not arrive earlier than usual.
explanation: If the rains came early, the earlier sowing would not beat them. Water needs, prices and other farmers do not matter to the plan.

stem: The town built a new bypass to reduce traffic in its centre, yet traffic in the centre increased. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Easier access to the shops drew more people into the centre.
The bypass was built using concrete and strong steel.
The bypass has two lanes in each direction for traffic and a footpath.
Heavy goods vehicles are the main users of the bypass.
explanation: If the bypass attracted more people to the centre, it could raise traffic there. The other options do not explain the rise.

stem: Farah says: 'The library's membership fell after it moved to a new building, so the move must have driven readers away.' Farah assumes that
options: the new building is harder to reach than the old one was.
most readers had been unhappy with the old building's facilities.
the library cut its opening hours after it moved.
membership would not have fallen anyway for some other reason.
explanation: To blame the move, Farah must rule out other causes of the fall. 'Libraries lose members whenever they move' is a general rule she does not need, and distance is not mentioned.

stem: No one has ever proved that the old well is unsafe to drink from. So the well must be safe. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
takes a lack of proof against a claim as proof that it is true
draws a general claim from a very small group
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
explanation: Nobody having proved it unsafe does not prove it safe; it may simply not have been tested.

stem: Statements: A firm has 40 employees. Of these, 25 can drive and 18 can speak English. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: At least 18 employees are unable to drive a car.
Exactly 3 employees can both drive and speak English in this firm.
No employee in the firm can do both of these things.
At least 3 employees can both drive and speak English.
explanation: 25 + 18 = 43, which exceeds 40, so at least 43 − 40 = 3 people are counted twice. 'Exactly 3' is not certain, since the overlap could be larger; and 40 − 25 = 15 cannot drive, not 18.

stem: Imran says: 'You must either support my plan fully or you are against the school.' The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
draws a general claim from a very small group
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
offers only two choices when more are possible
explanation: A person could support part of the plan, or disagree with it and still be loyal to the school.

stem: A government hospital added a second registration counter. A visitor concludes that patients now receive treatment sooner. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: The second counter was staffed by experienced clerks.
Most patients registered at the hospital are admitted as inpatients.
The hospital treats fewer patients now than it did last year.
Registration was a major part of the delay patients faced.
explanation: If long registration queues were not the main delay, a second counter would not speed up treatment. Appointments and extra doctors are different causes that the visitor does not mention.

stem: The government says banning plastic bags will cut litter in the city. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Plastic bags are very cheap and widely used by shops.
Some shops already give customers paper bags instead.
The ban is due to take effect from the very start of January.
Most litter in the city is food wrappers and bottles, not bags.
explanation: If bags make up little of the litter, banning them will not cut litter much.

stem: Bakeries in Gulberg open at 6 a.m. Fresh Bake is a bakery in Gulberg. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Fresh Bake sells the cheapest bread in Gulberg.
Fresh Bake closes at 6 p.m.
Fresh Bake is the oldest bakery in Gulberg.
Fresh Bake opens at 6 a.m.
explanation: Fresh Bake belongs to the group of Gulberg bakeries that open at 6 a.m. Price, closing time and age are not given.

stem: Statements: In Hira's class, everyone who takes drawing also takes music. Bilal does not take music. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Bilal takes drawing but not music.
Everyone who takes music takes drawing.
Bilal does not take drawing.
Hira takes drawing.
explanation: If Bilal took drawing he would take music, but he does not. So he does not take drawing. The reverse does not follow.

stem: Statements: All the buses on Route 5 are air-conditioned. Some buses on Route 5 are old. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Some old buses are air-conditioned.
All old buses are air-conditioned.
No bus on Route 5 is new.
Some air-conditioned buses are not on Route 5.
explanation: The old buses on Route 5 are air-conditioned, so some old buses are air-conditioned. The rest go beyond the statements.

stem: A town council says brighter paint on zebra crossings will cut pedestrian accidents. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Paint prices have risen sharply since last year.
Some pedestrians ignore zebra crossings altogether.
Zebra crossings are much shorter in the old part of town than elsewhere.
Pedestrian accidents fell only on streets where crossings were repainted.
explanation: The comparison between repainted and unchanged streets points to the paint as the cause. The other options do not.

stem: The city plans to build a flyover at its busiest crossing to reduce traffic jams. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The crossing is close to a busy mosque and a large vegetable market.
The flyover will cost less than a new signal system would.
The delays come mainly from vehicles crossing each other's paths.
The crossing is busier on Fridays than on any other day.
explanation: A flyover separates crossing streams of traffic, so it helps if the delays come from vehicles crossing paths. The other facts say nothing about why jams form.

stem: Ayesha's class scored higher this year, and she credits the new teaching method. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The new method relies on coloured charts and short videos.
A class with the same teacher and the old method showed no rise.
Ayesha's class is the largest class in the whole school.
Last year's class used the same textbooks as this year's.
explanation: A comparison group that did not change shows no rise, which supports the new method as the cause. The other options are irrelevant details.

stem: To reduce jams on the market road, the traffic police will stop rickshaws from entering it. The police assume that
options: rickshaws are an important cause of the jams on that road.
rickshaws are slower than all other vehicles on that road.
rickshaw drivers will use other roads to reach the market.
most shoppers reach the market in private cars.
explanation: Banning rickshaws can ease jams only if they contribute to the jams. Drivers' dislike of the road is irrelevant.

stem: Rizwan has put solar panels on his roof so that his monthly electricity bill will fall. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: The panels will receive enough sunlight to generate a useful amount of power.
Electricity prices in the country will keep rising over the next decade.
Rizwan's neighbours will also switch to solar power within a year.
The panels will last longer than most other household appliances.
explanation: The bill falls only if the panels actually produce power, which needs sunlight. Future tariffs and neighbours' choices have no bearing on that.

stem: Whenever ice-cream sales rise in Karachi, the number of people swimming at the beach also rises. A councillor concludes that eating ice cream makes people want to swim. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
offers only two choices when more are possible
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
explanation: Both may rise together because of hot weather. A link is not enough to show that one causes the other.

stem: A company plans a four-day working week. Its director says: 'A longer weekend will leave staff refreshed, so they will produce as much in four days as they now do in five.' The director assumes that
options: customers will accept slower service on the fifth day.
staff will use the extra day for training.
refreshed staff will work faster during the four days than they do now.
the office rent will fall with fewer working days.
explanation: Total output can only stay the same in four days if the pace rises. Service on a day off, training and rent are different matters.

stem: The city will charge a toll on the new bridge to repay its construction cost. The plan assumes that
options: the toll will be lower than the toll charged on any other bridge.
enough vehicles will still use the bridge once the toll is charged.
the cost of building the bridge was higher than expected.
the toll will be collected by the city's own staff.
explanation: Revenue from a toll depends on vehicles continuing to cross. Other bridges, wages and uniform rates are not needed for the argument.

stem: Some people who exercise regularly sleep badly. All people who sleep badly feel tired during the day. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Some people who exercise regularly feel tired during the day.
All people who exercise regularly feel tired during the day.
People who feel tired in the day always sleep badly at night.
No one who exercises regularly sleeps well at night.
explanation: The exercisers who sleep badly all feel tired, so some exercisers feel tired. 'All exercisers' and the reversal go beyond the statement.

stem: Sales of umbrellas rose in the city during the dry season, which had much less rain than usual. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Umbrellas were sold at higher prices during the wet season.
Many shoppers bought umbrellas to use against the strong sun.
Rainfall is rare in some other parts of the country.
Shops in the city stocked more umbrellas than before.
explanation: Using umbrellas as sunshades explains the sales without rain. The other options do not explain why sales rose.

stem: Rickshaw fares have risen twice this year, fuel prices keep climbing, and drivers report that their earnings are falling. The city should therefore consider reviewing the fares. Which of the following is the main conclusion of the passage?
options: Rickshaw fares have risen twice in the past year.
Fuel prices keep climbing and drivers' earnings are falling.
Rickshaw drivers should be paid a salary by the city.
The city should consider reviewing rickshaw fares.
explanation: The word 'therefore' marks the final claim: a fare review is needed. The other options are reasons or an unsupported comparison.

stem: Zain argues that learning to swim is useful for children living near a river. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The river is wider here than at most other places.
Swimming lessons are expensive for most local families.
Most drowning accidents in the area involve children who cannot swim.
Some children in the area enjoy fishing in the river.
explanation: If those who drown are mostly non-swimmers, learning to swim protects children. The other options do not connect swimming to safety.

stem: Every shop on Liberty Lane closes by 9 p.m. Bilal's shop is on Liberty Lane. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Bilal's shop opens before 9 a.m.
Bilal owns other shops on Liberty Lane.
All shops in the city close by 9 p.m.
Bilal's shop closes by 9 p.m.
explanation: Bilal's shop belongs to the group 'shops on Liberty Lane', all of which close by 9 p.m. The other options talk about opening time, ownership or the whole city, none of which is stated.

stem: A cricket coach says: 'Our fast bowlers take most of their wickets in the first ten overs, so we should give the new ball only to them.' The coach assumes that
options: the opponents' batsmen are weaker against spin bowlers than pace.
the match will last more than ten overs for each team.
spin bowlers will be rested if the new ball goes to the fast bowlers.
the new ball is the reason the fast bowlers take wickets early.
explanation: If the bowlers took early wickets for another reason, the new ball would add nothing. The coach does not need spinners to be useless early on.

stem: Sana says the new rule on school uniforms is unfair. The principal replies: 'You were late three times this month, so we need not take your complaint seriously.' The principal's reply is flawed because it
options: takes a lack of proof against a claim as proof that it is true
offers only two choices when more are possible
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim
assumes each part must share the traits of the whole
explanation: Sana's lateness has no bearing on whether the uniform rule is fair.

stem: Two towns have the same population, yet the first town has twice as many doctors per head of population as the second, and its people are no healthier. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: The first town has more hospitals and clinics than the second town has.
Doctors in the second town are paid lower salaries.
Both towns have a good number of schools and colleges.
Most of the first town's doctors treat patients from nearby villages.
explanation: If many doctors treat outsiders, the town's own residents do not receive twice as much care.

stem: Hira says the school canteen should sell fruit instead of chips because students will then be healthier. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Students who eat fruit daily fall ill less often than those who eat chips.
Chips cost less than fruit in the local market where students shop.
The canteen has sold chips to students for many years now.
Some students prefer fruit juice to both fruit and chips.
explanation: Fewer illnesses among fruit eaters supports the claim of better health. Price, history and packed lunches are not about health.

stem: Imran says the town's crime rate fell because of new street lights. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Crime fell equally in nearby towns that had no new lights.
The street lights use low-energy bulbs that last longer.
The town also repainted its main market last year.
The lights were installed in the month of March.
explanation: A similar fall where no lights were added suggests the lights were not the cause. The other options say nothing about whether the lights affected crime.

stem: Statements: Only employees with a card can enter the lab. Nida entered the lab. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: All employees with a card entered the lab.
Nida is the lab manager.
Nida entered the lab by mistake.
Nida is an employee with a card.
explanation: Only card-holding employees can enter, so Nida must be one. Nothing says every card holder entered.

stem: Statements: Most students in the hostel eat in the mess. Nobody who eats in the mess pays extra for dinner. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: All students in the hostel pay something for dinner.
Most students in the hostel do not pay extra for dinner.
Students who skip the mess are charged extra for dinner.
The mess serves dinner to every student each evening.
explanation: Most students eat in the mess, and none who eat there pay extra. So most do not pay extra. The other options go beyond the statements.

stem: A hospital hired more doctors, but patients' average waiting time grew. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Patient numbers grew faster than the number of doctors.
The doctors hired are well qualified and have years of experience.
The hospital is close to the main bus stand.
Some of the doctors work only during night hours.
explanation: If patient numbers grew faster than staffing, waits can rise despite more doctors.

stem: Citizens who live near parks report better sleep and lower stress than those who do not. The council therefore plans more parks in crowded areas. Which of the following is the main conclusion of the passage?
options: Citizens who live near parks report better sleep than others.
Crowded areas have more stress than areas near parks.
Parks should be built before houses are built.
The council should plan more parks in crowded areas.
explanation: The plan for more parks is what the reports are offered to justify. The reports are evidence, and the last option is not stated.

stem: A farmer says a scarecrow in the field will keep birds away. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The field grows wheat, which birds are known to eat.
The farmer lives in a house very close to the field.
The scarecrow is made of straw and the farmer's old clothes.
Birds in the area have been seen sitting on scarecrows.
explanation: Birds that perch on scarecrows are clearly not frightened by them.

stem: Students who read newspapers daily score higher in current affairs than those who do not. Hamza reads a newspaper daily. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Hamza will certainly score the highest marks in his class.
Newspapers are the only way to learn about current affairs.
Hamza will probably score higher than students who skip newspapers.
Students who skip newspapers always fail the current affairs paper.
explanation: The statement describes a tendency, so only a probable conclusion is safe. 'Certainly' and 'only way' overstate it.

stem: Each brick in the wall is small and light, so the wall must be small and light. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
assumes the whole must share the traits of each part
argues that a claim is true because many people believe it
explanation: A wall made of many small bricks can still be large and heavy; what holds for the parts need not hold for the whole.

stem: In a survey, 70 per cent of those who bought a laptop from Store X said they were satisfied. In the same survey, 85 per cent of those who bought from Store Y said they were satisfied. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Store Y's laptops are better made than those sold by Store X.
More laptops were sold by Store Y than by Store X.
Store X should improve its service to match Store Y.
Among those surveyed, Store Y's buyers were more often satisfied.
explanation: Only the percentages of satisfied buyers among those surveyed can be compared. Product quality, closing a store and sales numbers are not stated.

stem: An office manager proposes banning air conditioners to cut the office's electricity use. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Most of the office's electricity goes to computers and lights.
The office is on the third floor of an old building.
Staff in the office prefer to work in cooler rooms.
Air conditioners are expensive to buy and to repair.
explanation: If air conditioners use little of the power, banning them saves little.

stem: A shop reduced its prices yet its daily income fell. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: The shop stays open for business on Fridays as well as other days.
Other shops in the area sell the very same goods.
Customers fell in number by more than the price cuts could offset.
Vegetable prices in the area vary with the season.
explanation: Income is price times quantity; if sales volume fell by more than prices, income falls.

stem: The student council president says: 'More students came to the sports day than to the debate, so students value sports more than debating.' The president assumes that
options: sports days always attract more students than debates.
attendance shows how much students value an event.
the debate was held on a working day.
students who came to the debate disliked it.
explanation: Attendance is treated as a measure of value, which is the hidden step. Other reasons for low turnout would weaken the claim, not support it.

stem: Statements: Fatima is taller than Zara. Zara is taller than Hina. Sana is shorter than Hina. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Sana is taller than Zara.
Fatima is taller than Sana.
Hina is the tallest of the four.
Zara and Sana are the same height.
explanation: Fatima > Zara > Hina > Sana in height, so Fatima is taller than Sana. The other options contradict this order.

stem: Bilal's start-up argues that delivering groceries by motorbike will be faster than delivering by van in the crowded old city. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: In narrow old-city streets, motorbikes take less time than vans.
Vans can carry far more groceries than a motorbike can.
Motorbikes use much less fuel than vans over exactly the same distance.
Most grocery orders in the old city arrive in the evening.
explanation: The claim is about speed in crowded streets, so the option on journey times supports it directly. Capacity and fuel are other issues.

stem: A company says flexible working hours will reduce the number of staff who leave. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Many who left said fixed hours were their main reason for leaving.
The company has offices in two different cities.
Some staff prefer to work from home on certain days.
The company hired more new staff last year than before.
explanation: If fixed hours drive staff away, flexible hours should keep them. The other options say nothing about reasons for leaving.

stem: Ayesha says the school should not extend the library hours. Bilal replies: 'Ayesha never reads anything, so her opinion does not count.' Bilal's reply is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim
draws a general claim from a very small group
offers only two choices when more are possible
explanation: Bilal attacks Ayesha herself, not her argument about library hours.

stem: A mobile app has a high download count but few daily users. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: The app is free to download from the main app stores.
Many people install the app out of curiosity and soon stop using it.
The app's icon is blue with a large white letter on it, like others.
The developer of the app lives and works in Lahore.
explanation: Curiosity downloads that are not followed by regular use explain both facts.

stem: A school plans a homework-free weekend to improve students' wellbeing. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Homework-free weekends are already common in some other countries today.
Trial students with homework-free weekends felt less stressed on Mondays.
Teachers in the school prefer to set homework on Fridays.
The school has a large sports ground and a library.
explanation: Reduced stress in a trial is direct evidence for improved wellbeing. A custom elsewhere does not show that it works.

stem: Statements: A shop gives a discount only on purchases above Rs 2,000. Sana got a discount. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Every purchase above Rs 2,000 gets a discount.
Sana bought more than Rs 5,000 of goods.
Sana's purchase was above Rs 2,000.
The shop gives discounts every day.
explanation: Since a discount is given only above Rs 2,000, Sana's purchase must have been above it. The shop might give no discount on some large purchases, so the first option is not supported.

stem: Maryam says: 'The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow, so the picnic should be cancelled.' Maryam assumes that
options: the picnic cannot be held in the rain.
it has rained every day this week.
the forecast was shown on television.
the picnic is the school's first outing.
explanation: Cancelling makes sense only if the picnic needs dry weather. Past weather, where the forecast appeared and the outing's history do not matter to the argument.

stem: A health body says drinking water before meals helps people eat less. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Water is available free of charge in most homes and offices in the city.
Many people drink tea rather than water after meals.
Some people feel thirsty before meals in the summer.
A study found water-drinkers ate fewer calories than a similar group.
explanation: A comparison with a similar group directly supports the claim. The other options are unrelated to how much people eat.

stem: The city's metro bus lane is empty for much of the day, so a councillor proposes opening it to private cars outside peak hours. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: Most private car owners would use the lane during off-peak hours.
The metro buses already run at a loss during off-peak hours.
Allowing cars in would not seriously slow the metro buses.
Drivers will pay a small fee for using the bus lane.
explanation: The proposal works only if the buses keep moving freely once cars are allowed in. Running costs and who uses the bus are not part of the reasoning.

stem: Mobile data prices have fallen, so a telecom analyst predicts more people will make video calls. The analyst assumes that
options: most smartphone owners already make video calls every day.
telecom companies will advertise video calls more heavily.
high prices were keeping some people from making video calls.
video calls are cheaper than voice calls in most countries of the world.
explanation: A price fall helps only if price was a barrier. 'Everyone owns a smartphone' goes beyond what is needed.

stem: Hamza says the corner shop does well because it opens late at night. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The shop's owner has two brothers who help him.
Most of the shop's sales happen after 9 p.m.
The shop sells cold drinks and snacks all year.
The shop is the oldest one on the corner.
explanation: If most sales come after 9 p.m., late opening is clearly important. The other facts do not.

stem: Every time Hira wears her blue shirt to a match, her team wins. She concludes that her blue shirt makes her team win. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: assumes each part must share the traits of the whole
offers only two choices when more are possible
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
explanation: The wins coincide with the shirt, but nothing shows the shirt has any effect.

stem: The cricket ground has floodlights, so the club secretary says evening matches can be played there. The secretary assumes that
options: the club will sell tickets for evening matches at a higher price.
evening temperatures will be cooler than they are during the day.
the floodlights will be switched on and work properly.
the players will be able to practise during the day as well.
explanation: Lights that are off or broken would not allow evening play. Crowd size and the ground's size are irrelevant to whether play is possible.

stem: Hira says: 'Banning phones in the classroom will raise exam results, because students will pay more attention.' Hira assumes that
options: paying more attention helps students score higher marks.
most students currently use their phones for games during lessons.
teachers will be able to teach faster once phones are banned.
parents will support the ban once they see the exam results.
explanation: The step from 'more attention' to 'better results' is the hidden link. 'Every student' is too strong, since the ban could help even if only some students were distracted.

stem: A transport authority argues that cutting metro bus fares will raise the number of passengers. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Earlier fare cuts on other routes were followed by more passengers.
Metro buses are cleaner and more comfortable than minibuses.
The authority has a large number of staff and buses.
Fares on private minibuses are already very low.
explanation: A similar earlier case in which a fare cut raised passenger numbers supports the prediction. The other options do not show a link between fares and passengers.

stem: The city plans a flyover at its busiest crossing to reduce traffic jams. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The crossing is close to a school and a large hospital.
Flyovers are now common in most large cities of the world.
The flyover will have two lanes in each direction.
The flyover would end at a narrow road with long queues.
explanation: Traffic would pile up where the flyover ends, so jams would simply move. The other options do not show that.

stem: Plants kept near a sunny window grew taller than plants kept in a dark corner, although both groups received the same water. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Plants kept in a dark corner will always stop growing.
Sunlight probably helped the plants near the window grow taller.
The amount of water given matters more than sunlight.
Taller plants are always healthier than shorter ones.
explanation: Water was equal, so sunlight is the likely difference. The other options make claims the experiment does not support.

stem: Kamran says his team won because he changed the batting order. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The match began at ten o'clock in the morning.
Kamran has captained the team for the last two years.
The opposing team was missing its two best bowlers.
The ground had been newly prepared for the match.
explanation: Another good reason for the win, the weak opposition attack, reduces the case for the batting order.

stem: A bakery sold fewer cakes during the month of Ramadan, though its overall sales rose. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Customers bought many more dates and samosas for iftar.
Cakes are baked fresh each morning in the bakery.
The bakery recently installed a new, larger oven.
The bakery opens its doors at seven in the morning.
explanation: A rise in other items can raise total sales even when cake sales fall.

stem: Nida says her cousin's shop should stock more school stationery in April because the new session starts then. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The shop sells sweets and snacks as well as stationery and toys.
In previous years, the shop's stationery sales were highest in April.
April has more working days than most other months.
Schools in the area close for winter break in January.
explanation: Past sales peaking in April back up the advice. The other options give no link between April and demand.

stem: After a campaign encouraging people to wear helmets, the number of riders treated at a hospital for head injuries went up, although motorcycle accidents did not increase. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Helmets are now sold in many different colours.
More riders wear helmets, so some once-fatal injuries now reach hospital.
Motorcycle sales rose slightly during the campaign.
The hospital treats many kinds of injury besides head injuries and burns.
explanation: Helmets can turn fatal head injuries into survivable ones, so more patients reach hospital. The other options do not explain the rise.

stem: The school library is open on all weekdays. Today is Wednesday. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: The school library is open on Sundays.
The library has no books on Wednesday.
The school library is open today.
The library is open all night.
explanation: Wednesday is a weekday, and the library is open on all weekdays. The other options go beyond the statement.

stem: Usman's marks rose after he began using a revision app, and his sister says the app was the cause. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The app contains lessons in mathematics, science and English.
Usman studies in the evening after he returns home.
Classmates who never used the app improved just as much.
The app can be used without an internet connection.
explanation: If non-users improved equally, something else, not the academy, explains the rise. The other options do not undermine the claim.

stem: A salesman says his tonic cures colds, since customers recover within a week of taking it. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The tonic is sold in glass bottles of two different sizes.
Most colds clear up within a week without any treatment.
The salesman travels between several towns each month.
Some customers buy two bottles of the tonic at once.
explanation: If colds pass in a week anyway, recovery shows nothing about the tonic.

stem: An airline says a faster check-in will increase passenger satisfaction. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Most passengers said delays at the boarding gate annoy them most.
The airline flies to twelve cities in six countries.
Check-in desks open three hours before each flight.
The airline recently changed its logo and uniforms.
explanation: If check-in is not what upsets passengers, speeding it up will not raise satisfaction much.

stem: A researcher says a new fertiliser raises wheat yields. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: In a trial on equal fields, the fertilised one gave more wheat.
The fertiliser is sold in bags of fifty kilograms each.
Farmers using the fertiliser also spend more on better seed.
Wheat prices were unusually high in the year of the trial.
explanation: A controlled comparison isolates the fertiliser's effect. Bag size, seed spending and prices do not.

stem: Each player in the team is an excellent batsman, so the team must be an excellent batting side. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: takes a lack of proof against a claim as proof that it is true
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
offers only two choices when more are possible
assumes the whole must share the traits of each part
explanation: A team of excellent individuals may bat badly together; what is true of each part need not be true of the whole.

stem: A study finds that pet owners are happier, so a councillor suggests giving free pets to lonely elderly people to make them happier. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Pets need regular feeding and visits to the vet.
Some pets live for fifteen years or even longer.
Cats are more popular as household pets than dogs in most cities.
Happy people are more likely to keep pets in the first place.
explanation: If happiness leads to pet ownership, rather than the other way round, giving pets to unhappy people may not help.

stem: The village farmers planted more wheat this year, but the total harvest was smaller than last year's. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: A drought destroyed much of the crop.
Wheat is the main crop of the region.
Farmers sell their wheat at the market.
Wheat flour is used for roti.
explanation: A drought would reduce the harvest even when more land was sown.

stem: A principal believes the school's tree-planting week will make students more aware of the environment. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The school has a large playground and a small farm.
Tree-planting week is usually held in March each year.
Students in similar weeks elsewhere became more careful about waste.
Saplings can be bought cheaply from the local nursery.
explanation: A similar case where participation raised environmental care supports the belief. The rest are unrelated.

stem: All members of the school's debating club have represented the school at least once. Sana has never represented the school. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Sana wants to join the debating club.
Sana is not a member of the debating club.
Sana is a poor speaker.
No one but club members has represented the school.
explanation: If Sana were a member she would have represented the school; she has not, so she is not a member. The last option reverses the statement, which does not say that only members represented the school.

stem: A principal says the new library raised reading levels because reading test scores rose this year. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The library has air-conditioning and comfortable chairs.
The school has about six hundred students in total.
The new library opened to students in the month of January.
This year's reading test was much easier than last year's.
explanation: An easier test could explain higher scores without any real improvement.

stem: The newspaper is reliable because it prints the truth. We know it prints the truth because it is a reliable newspaper. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
draws a general claim from a very small group
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
explanation: Each claim is used to support the other, so nothing independent supports either.

stem: A planner says electric rickshaws let fares be cut without harming the drivers' incomes. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Electric rickshaws are much quieter than petrol rickshaws.
Petrol rickshaws have been in use for many decades.
Electric rickshaw drivers spend far less on fuel and repairs.
Passengers generally prefer riding in newer vehicles.
explanation: Lower running costs leave room for lower fares without lowering income. Noise and popularity do not.

stem: A bank notes that most customers who open accounts online never visit a branch. It also notes that branch visits have fallen sharply over the last five years. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Banks plan to close most of their branches in the next year.
Online account opening is likely one reason for fewer branch visits.
Customers who open accounts online earn more interest than others.
Branch visits fell because staff became less helpful.
explanation: The two facts together point to a link between online opening and fewer visits. Closing branches, dislike of staff and interest rates are not supported.

stem: Statements: The library lends books for two weeks. Zain borrowed a book on 3 March and returned it on 20 March. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Zain kept the book longer than the lending period.
Zain borrowed more than one book from the library.
Zain has already paid a fine to the library.
Zain borrowed the book on behalf of a close friend.
explanation: 3 March to 20 March is 17 days, which is more than two weeks. A fine is not mentioned.

stem: The municipal committee will plant 500 trees along the canal road. The chairman says the road will therefore be cooler in summer. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: No other road in the city needs trees.
The canal road is the longest road in the city.
The trees will grow large enough to give shade.
Summer temperatures will fall in the whole city.
explanation: Cooling the road depends on the trees giving shade, and young saplings do not do that. How many other roads need trees, or how long the road is, makes no difference to the claim.

stem: Rabia says she will become fit by walking for ten minutes each day. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Doctors say at least thirty minutes of daily exercise is needed.
Rabia lives close to a park with a walking track.
Walking is one of the most popular forms of exercise for adults.
Rabia's friend also goes walking every morning.
explanation: If ten minutes is too short to help, Rabia's plan will not work.

stem: Millions of people use this brand of toothpaste, so it must be the best toothpaste. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
argues that a claim is true because many people believe it
offers only two choices when more are possible
assumes each part must share the traits of the whole
explanation: Popularity does not show quality.

stem: Bilal's marks improved sharply after he joined an evening academy. His father concludes that the academy caused the improvement. The father assumes that
options: the academy is better than every other academy in the city.
nothing else important changed in Bilal's studies at the same time.
Bilal's father has closely studied the academy's teaching methods and fees.
the academy gives more homework than Bilal's school does.
explanation: Blaming the academy only works if no other change, such as more self-study, explains the rise. 'Every student improves' is far stronger than the father needs and is not required.

stem: Statements: Every rose in Ahmed's garden is red. Ahmed's garden has no tulips. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Ahmed's garden has nothing but red roses in it.
Every red flower in the world is a rose.
No red flower in the garden is a tulip.
Ahmed grows red roses because he likes red.
explanation: The garden has no tulips, so no red flower there is a tulip. The garden might contain other flowers too.

stem: A mosque committee wants to collect rainwater in a tank to cut its water bill. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Most of the mosque's water bill is for washing, which rainwater can meet.
The mosque's courtyard is large enough for a big storage tank.
Rainwater tanks last longer than most other water systems.
The mosque is visited by many people on Fridays and during Ramadan.
explanation: The plan saves money only if the main use of water can be met by rainwater, which the correct option says. The other options do not link rainwater to the bill.

stem: Thirty-five of the fifty students in Class 10 attended revision sessions and all of them passed. The teacher concludes that revision sessions raise the pass rate. The teacher assumes that
options: the students who attended were no stronger than those who did not.
the revision sessions were held on the days just before the test.
students who attend revision sessions enjoy school more than others.
the fifteen students who did not attend would have failed anyway.
explanation: If the keenest students attended, their success may have another cause. The conclusion is safe only if the two groups were comparable to begin with; the other options do not address that.

stem: A college says its new timetable will let students sleep longer, so their grades will improve. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The new timetable begins in September every year.
Students have used the extra time for jobs instead of sleep.
Classes are fifty minutes long in the new timetable, with short breaks.
The college has a hostel for out-of-town students.
explanation: If students are not sleeping longer, the chain from timetable to better grades breaks.

stem: A mobile app shows that the number of users who finish its lessons doubled after the lessons were shortened to five minutes. The developer says: 'Shorter lessons keep users engaged.' Which of the following is the main conclusion of the passage?
options: The number of users who finish lessons doubled.
Shorter lessons keep users engaged.
Lessons were shortened to five minutes.
The developer has made a mobile app.
explanation: The developer's own claim is the point the figures are used to support. The other options are the evidence.

stem: The number of students who walk to school has fallen every year since the school bus service began. The principal says the bus service is the reason. Which of the following is the main conclusion of the passage?
options: The bus service is the reason fewer students walk to school.
The number of students walking has fallen every year.
The school began running a bus service for its students.
The principal is personally responsible for running the bus service.
explanation: The principal's claim of cause is the conclusion; the rest is background or evidence.

stem: A school's pass rate rose, yet fewer of its students were admitted to universities. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: The school added a new classroom block this year.
Several experienced teachers retired from the school this year.
A new rule raised the marks required for university admission.
More students joined the school from other cities.
explanation: If universities demanded higher marks, a higher pass rate could still lead to fewer admissions.

stem: The medicine has been used for ten years and no study has shown that it causes harm. The health minister concludes that the medicine is completely harmless. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
takes a lack of proof against a claim as proof that it is true
draws a general claim from a very small group
argues that a claim is true because many people believe it
explanation: That no harm has been shown does not prove it is harmless, as harm may simply not have been studied.

stem: Ahmed's bakery has put up a large signboard on the main road. The owner says sales will now rise because more passers-by will notice the shop. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: Rival bakeries on the same road will not put up bigger signboards.
The owner will be able to bake more bread if sales increase.
The cost of the signboard will be recovered within a single month.
Some of the people who notice the signboard will buy from the shop.
explanation: For more notice to mean more sales, at least some of those who notice must actually buy. The other options are about rivals, prices or advertising costs, which the argument does not need.

stem: Asad asked three of his neighbours about the new bus route, and all three liked it. He says that everyone in the city likes the new route. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
treats a needed condition as if it were enough
draws a general claim from a very small group
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
explanation: Three neighbours are too few, and may not represent the whole city.

stem: A researcher says chess improves logical thinking and so raises mathematics marks. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: Teenagers who play chess also enjoy reading more than others.
Chess clubs usually meet after school on weekdays.
Teenagers randomly given chess lessons improved more in mathematics.
Schools with chess boards have higher mathematics marks.
explanation: Random assignment rules out the explanation that stronger students simply choose chess. The other options show only association.

stem: A council says new dustbins have made its streets cleaner. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The new bins are painted green and fitted with lids.
The council already sends cleaners out to the main streets every morning.
A bigger cleaning campaign is planned for next year.
Litter fell on streets given new bins but not on streets without them.
explanation: A fall only where bins were added, with no change elsewhere, links the bins to the improvement. The other options do not.

stem: An online store promises delivery within one day in Lahore. The manager says customers in Lahore will therefore prefer this store to its rivals. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: Rival stores in Lahore take at least a week to deliver orders.
The store's prices are lower than its rivals' prices in every city.
Customers in Lahore care about how quickly goods arrive.
Most customers in Lahore have never shopped online before.
explanation: Fast delivery can win customers only if they value it. The argument says nothing about rivals' prices, customers' shopping habits or other cities.

stem: A juice company says its drink improves concentration, since students who drank it scored higher in a test. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Students who chose the drink also slept and studied more.
The drink comes in three flavours and two sizes.
The juice is made from fresh oranges grown in the nearby region.
The test lasted two hours and had fifty questions.
explanation: If those students had other advantages, the drink may not explain the scores. The other options do not offer another explanation.

stem: A pharmacy advertises: 'Our vitamin tablets are made from natural ingredients, so they are safe to take.' The advertisement assumes that
options: customers trust pharmacies more than they trust doctors.
anything made from natural ingredients is safe to take.
natural ingredients cost more than synthetic ones.
tablets are safer than vitamins taken in syrup form.
explanation: The link between 'natural' and 'safe' is the hidden premise, and it is not always true. The other options do not connect the premise to the conclusion.

stem: The city's water supply is cut for two hours every morning. Households that own storage tanks do not run out of water, while those without tanks often do. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: Households with tanks use less water than those without them.
The morning cut affects only households that own tanks.
Storage tanks help households cope with the morning cut.
The water supply will be restored in the coming months.
explanation: Tank owners avoid shortages, so tanks help. The other options bring in water use, future plans and family size, which the passage does not mention.

stem: Statements: Mangoes and guavas are sold at Karim's stall. Guavas are cheaper than mangoes. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Karim sells fruit that is cheaper than mangoes.
Karim sells more guavas than mangoes every day.
Karim's stall is the cheapest stall in the market.
Karim sells no fruit other than mangoes and guavas.
explanation: Guavas are sold there and are cheaper than mangoes, so at least one fruit sold is cheaper than mangoes.

stem: Sana argues that a village needs a new clinic because many residents must travel over 20 km to see a doctor. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The village has a primary school and a small market.
Some residents skip needed treatment because of the distance.
The nearest hospital is large and well equipped.
Many residents own bicycles or motorbikes.
explanation: People skipping needed treatment shows the distance is harming them, which supports a nearer clinic. The hospital's equipment does not show a need for a new clinic.

stem: To get a place in medical college, a student must score high marks in the entry test. Fatima scored high marks in the entry test, so she will get a place. The reasoning above is flawed because it
options: treats a needed condition as if it were enough
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
offers only two choices when more are possible
draws a general claim from a very small group
explanation: High marks are required but may not be enough, as there may be limited seats or other requirements.

stem: Zara says that advertisements for a tuition centre on buses will raise enrolment. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The centre teaches several subjects at different levels.
Most students the centre wants never travel by bus.
Bus advertisements are cheaper than newspaper advertisements.
The centre opened its first branch only last year.
explanation: If the target students do not see the ads, the ads cannot raise enrolment.

stem: The owner of a sweet shop says a large new banner outside will bring more customers because more people will notice the shop. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The banner is blue and white with large gold letters.
Trees block the banner from the view of passers-by.
The shop sells fresh sweets every day of the week.
The owner's brother runs a bigger sweet shop nearby.
explanation: If passers-by cannot see the signboard, it cannot bring in customers. The other options leave the argument untouched.

stem: Hamza sleeps eight hours every night, yet he feels tired all day. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: Hamza likes to read books before going to bed.
Hamza travels to school by bus every morning.
He wakes up several times each night and sleeps lightly.
Hamza drinks a big cup of strong tea every morning.
explanation: Broken, light sleep can leave a person tired even after eight hours in bed.

stem: The tourism board plans an advertising campaign to bring more visitors to the northern valleys in winter. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Heavy snow closes the roads to the valleys in winter.
The valleys are very popular with visitors in summer.
The campaign will include television advertisements.
Many visitors travel to the valleys with their families.
explanation: If visitors cannot reach the valleys in winter, advertising cannot bring more of them. Summer popularity does not affect winter visits.

stem: A school will serve a free lunch so that fewer students are absent on exam days. The school assumes that
options: the school's canteen currently sells food at unfair prices.
students who eat lunch at school score higher marks.
some students stay away because they cannot get a meal.
no student will bring food from home once lunch is free.
explanation: A free lunch can only reduce absences if hunger or cost is one reason students stay away. 'All students skip lunch' is far stronger than needed.

stem: No student in the physics group failed the practical test. Some students in the chemistry group failed it. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?
options: All students in the chemistry group failed the practical test.
Students in the physics group are better than others at chemistry practicals.
Some students in the chemistry group are not in the physics group.
No student in the chemistry group took the practical test.
explanation: A chemistry student who failed cannot be in the physics group, since no physics student failed. So some chemistry students are outside it. The other options go beyond the statements.

stem: Workers who attend a two-day safety workshop have fewer accidents than other workers, so a factory manager decides to send everyone to it. The manager assumes that
options: the workshop teaches skills that cannot be learned on the job.
the workers who attend were not already safer than the rest.
no worker will be hurt while attending the workshop itself.
the factory had no safety training of any kind before this.
explanation: If the careful workers were the ones who chose to attend, the workshop may not be the reason for fewer accidents. Cost and enjoyment do not affect the logic.

stem: Statements: If it rains, the match will be cancelled. The match was not cancelled. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: It rained heavily.
It did not rain.
The match was played in the rain.
The match will be played again.
explanation: If it had rained the match would have been cancelled. It was not, so it did not rain.

stem: Statements: Some engineers are musicians. All musicians are early risers. No early riser is late for work. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
options: Some engineers are never late for work.
All engineers belong to the group of early risers.
No musician in the group works as an engineer.
Some early risers are not musicians at all.
explanation: The engineers who are musicians are early risers, so are never late. The other options do not follow.

stem: A company's profits rose sharply in a year when its sales fell. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
options: The company cut its costs by more than the loss in sales revenue.
The company sells electronic goods and appliances.
Its main competitors also reported lower sales in that same year.
The company's head office is in the city of Islamabad.
explanation: Profit is revenue minus cost; a larger cost cut than revenue loss raises profit.

stem: The number of mobile phone shops in a market has doubled, so an analyst says the demand for phones has doubled. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Some of the new shops are on the first floor of the market.
Many new shops sell only accessories; phone sales are unchanged.
Phone prices differ a great deal from shop to shop in the market.
The market is open on Sundays as well as weekdays.
explanation: Unchanged phone sales show that demand has not doubled, whatever the number of shops.

stem: A library will remove late fees so that more people borrow books. The library assumes that
options: most people who borrow books return them on the due date.
the library will earn more money without late fees.
late fees are the main income of the library.
late fees currently put some people off borrowing.
explanation: Removing a barrier can increase borrowing only if the barrier was keeping some people away. 'Every borrower returns books late' is far too strong.
